findings.title: The light-theme color was changed from the original 30% to 70%
findings.body: The embedded-post author link previously used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, but the new `dark-light-choose` light-theme branch uses 70%. This changes the appearance of this link on every non-dark theme, rather than only selecting an appropriate `$secondary`-based value for dark themes. Keep the original 30% primary value and use the corresponding dark-theme secondary value (as is done for comparable username links).

findings.title: Group member names lose their intended light-theme emphasis
findings.body: The `.group-member-info .name` rule previously used `$primary` at 30% lightness, but the change replaces its light-theme branch with `$primary` at 50%. Consequently, group member names render differently in light themes even though this change should only correct dark-theme colors. Preserve the 30% primary branch and use the appropriate `$secondary` branch for dark themes.

findings.title: Mobile group member names lose their intended light-theme emphasis
findings.body: The mobile `.group-member-info .name` rule previously used `$primary` at 30% lightness, while the new light-theme branch uses 50%. This regresses the existing light-theme rendering and also makes mobile inconsistent with the intended username/name styling. The light branch should remain 30% primary, with a secondary-based dark branch.

findings.title: Custom message length hint uses reversed lightness choices
findings.body: This rule previously used `$primary` at 70% lightness. The replacement changes the light-theme value to 30% primary and chooses 70% secondary for dark themes, reversing the expected polarity in both modes. The desktop version of the same `.custom-message-length` rule uses 70% primary / 30% secondary; mobile should use the same values so the hint remains consistently muted and legible.

findings.title: Mobile topic-map heading was changed to the wrong lightness level
findings.body: `.topic-map h3` previously used `$primary` at 20% lightness, but this patch changes it to 50% for the light-theme branch and 50% secondary for dark themes. This is not a secondary substitution of the original color; it changes the heading contrast in light themes and does not match the desktop topic-map heading, which uses 20% primary / 80% secondary. Retain the 20%/80% pairing.
